chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Bajali and al-Sindi ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When do you depart from Arafat?' He said, 'When the redness (of sunset) has passed from here,' and he pointed with his hand towards the east and the rising place of the sun.

key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: the redness (referring to the twilight after sunset)
key_terms.مَطْلَعِ الشَّمْسِ: the rising place of the sun

ai.seo_question: When should the pilgrim depart from Arafat according to the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the specific temporal marker for the departure from Arafat, linking the ritual act of Ifadah to the natural phenomenon of the sunset's redness fading. By pointing towards the east, the Imam clarifies the direction of the sun's setting, providing a practical, observable criterion for pilgrims to determine the exact moment to proceed to Muzdalifah, thereby grounding the legal ruling in clear physical signs.
